chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man contracts his owned slave and emancipates him, and he knows that for him is wealth, and the master did not exclude the wealth when he emancipated him, then it is for the slave.

key_terms.كِتَابَة: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a sum to gain freedom

ai.seo_question: What happens to a slave's wealth if the master frees him without explicitly excluding it?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Sadiq, clarifies the default legal presumption in kitabah contracts: unless the master explicitly reserves the slave's existing wealth, it automatically becomes the slave's property upon emancipation. This ruling underscores the principle of preserving the freed slave's financial independence and is a key reference in Shia jurisprudence for interpreting the silence of the master as consent to the transfer of assets.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man contracts his owned slave, and emancipates him, and he knows that for him would be wealth, and did not happen to make an exclusion for the wealth when he emancipated him, so it is for the slave’.
